title: The EU can now inspect AI models, block market access, and fine providers 3% of turnover. The grace period is over.
excerpt: EU AI Act enforcement powers took effect August 2. The Commission can evaluate models before release, restrict access, and fine up to 3% of global turnover or €15M.
content_html:
TL;DR

EU AI Act enforcement powers took effect August 2. The Commission can demand model evaluations, restrict market access, and fine providers up to 3% of global revenue. Applies to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google regardless of where they are based.

The European Commission gained enforcement powers over general-purpose AI models on August 2, ending the grace period for Chapter V of the EU AI Act. The Commission can now demand to evaluate models before regional release, restrict EU market access, and fine providers up to €15 million or 3% of global annual turnover, whichever is higher. The powers apply to any company offering a general-purpose AI model in the EU, regardless of where it is headquartered. Non-EU providers must appoint an EU-based authorised representative.

“A US address does not put a lab outside the EU regulator’s reach,” said Elisabetta Righini, partner at Sidley Austin. She added that liability extends beyond substantive breaches: “Refusing an information request, giving misleading answers, or blocking a model evaluation is finable on its own.” The Commission is in talks with OpenAI and Anthropic after recent cyber incidents involving their models, Reuters reported. The EU had sought access to Anthropic’s Mythos model for months before the company agreed to share it in June.

The timing raises transatlantic tensions. Trump threatened the EU with “substantial” tariffs after Brussels fined Google $1 billion in July under Digital Markets Act rules. Adding AI Act enforcement to that dynamic gives Brussels another lever against American tech companies. Anthropic’s silence on open weights drew accusations that it wanted regulatory protection, and EU enforcement gives the Commission tools to demand the kind of model access Anthropic was reluctant to provide voluntarily.

“We’ve collaborated closely with the European Commission and the wider ecosystem on implementing the AI Act,” said Tom Gordon, VP of EMEA policy at OpenAI. Google said it remains “dedicated to meeting all applicable rules.” The White House is also asserting control over who accesses frontier models, and American AI labs now face two governments demanding pre-release review from opposite sides of the Atlantic, each with its own thresholds, timelines, and penalties. The companies that built models to serve the world are discovering that the world wants to approve them first.

content_html_zh:
TL;DR

欧盟人工智能法案执行权于 8 月 2 日生效。 委员会可以要求模型评估、限制市场准入，并对提供商处以最高全球收入 3% 的罚款。 适用于 OpenAI、Anthropic、Google，无论它们位于何处。

欧盟委员会于 8 月 2 日获得了对通用人工智能模型的执法权，结束了《欧盟人工智能法案》第五章的宽限期。 委员会现在可以要求在区域发布之前对模型进行评估，限制欧盟市场准入，并对提供商处以最高 1500 万欧元或全球年营业额 3% 的罚款，以较高者为准。 这些权力适用于在欧盟提供通用人工智能模型的任何公司，无论其总部位于何处。 非欧盟提供商必须任命一名驻欧盟的授权代表。

盛德国际律师事务所合伙人 Elisabetta Righini 表示：“美国地址并不会将实验室置于欧盟监管机构的监管范围之外。” 她补充说，责任不仅仅限于实质性违规：“拒绝信息请求、提供误导性答案或阻止模型评估本身就是可被罚款的。” 据路透社报道，在最近发生涉及 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 模型的网络事件后，委员会正在与 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 进行谈判。 几个月来，欧盟一直在寻求使用 Anthropic 的 Mythos 模型，直到该公司于 6 月份同意分享该模型。

这一时机加剧了大西洋两岸的紧张局势。 7 月，布鲁塞尔根据《数字市场法》规定对谷歌处以 10 亿美元罚款后，特朗普威胁欧盟征收“巨额”关税。 在这一动态中加入《人工智能法案》的执行，为布鲁塞尔提供了对抗美国科技公司的另一个杠杆。 Anthropic 对开放权重的沉默招致了其想要监管保护的指责，而欧盟的执法为委员会提供了要求 Anthropic 不愿意自愿提供的模型访问权限的工具。

OpenAI 欧洲、中东和非洲政策副总裁 Tom Gordon 表示：“我们与欧盟委员会和更广泛的生态系统密切合作，实施《人工智能法案》。” 谷歌表示，它仍然“致力于遵守所有适用的规则”。 白宫还声称对谁可以访问前沿模型进行控制，美国人工智能实验室现在面临大西洋两岸两国政府要求的预发布审查，每个政府都有自己的门槛、时间表和处罚。 那些为世界服务而构建模型的公司发现，世界希望首先批准它们。
